name: Muse-Glimmer 30B
summary: A dense multimodal family with banked BF16 service evidence, a closed four-card Q8/WOQ plus DFlash record, and separate measured quantization, topology, metric-accounting, and quality boundaries.

architecture.class: dense causal transformer plus perception encoder
architecture.draft: DFlash assistant: 5 layers, block size 16, target-verified proposals

transfer_scope.status: shared architecture; each target quantization, draft artifact, topology, and modality requires its own gate
transfers: Muse-Glimmer llama.cpp model registration and tensor geometry
the family-specific attention, vision, and draft-feature plumbing where the same tensor path is independently exercised
does_not_transfer: BF16 exactness to Q8 or kquant target weights
Q8/WOQ speed to the BF16 service
text-only Q8 record quality to vision/mmproj
first-100 throughput to full-natural completion throughput
fleet aggregate throughput to single-request latency

b70_fit.basis: BF16 service uses two two-card replicas; the promoted UD-Q8_K_XL plus BF16 draft record uses TP4. Single-card near-lossless plus draft is fit-blocked on the measured envelope.

quality_evidence.scope: BF16 deterministic controls and target-verified Q8/DFlash task gates; Q8 is not lossless or universally token-exact, and the kquant quality tier is external rather than a lab quality gate

popularity.reason: No dated family-level popularity snapshot is stored.

family_closures.reason: The near-lossless target and DFlash buffers exceed the measured single-card memory envelope; reopening requires a source-level memory reduction.
The final exact kernel stack reached a 64.012 tok/s three-class mean. The original lossless BF16 century objective remained unmet and was not retroactively satisfied by the Q8 successor.
